BERT4Rec trains masked-item reconstruction and predicts the next item from an appended mask; the authors also train last-position masks to reduce this mismatch. For random-prefix endpoint training, implementation inference: sample target index t from training interactions, use only history before t, retain its latest L−1 items, append the reserved mask, then left-pad to L. Read the final mask position, never nonpadding_count−1. Including the target or later interactions in the bidirectional input leaks information. Uniform sampling over endpoints differs from uniform sampling over lengths followed by random cropping; specify the distribution explicitly because it changes target frequency and context lengths. Random-prefix sampling is an adaptation, whereas the original implementation uses sliding windows plus random and terminal masking. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690), [author implementation](https://github.com/FeiSun/BERT4Rec/blob/master/gen_data_fin.py).

Repeated item IDs in earlier history are legitimate context, not leakage: mask the target occurrence and preserve chronological repetitions. For sampled-negative training, explicitly exclude the positive ID, padding and mask token; excluding only visible prefix IDs can still sample the withheld positive. Excluding all known training positives reduces contradictions involving observed positives, but changes the negative distribution and cannot eliminate unknown false negatives. Do not inspect held-out labels to construct exclusions. Deduplicate sampled candidates when distinct negatives are intended; in-batch negatives also need positive-ID collision handling. The original model uses full-softmax training, while its evaluation code has separate candidate-sampling logic—these are different mechanisms. Preserve RecHarness’s pinned 99 unique negatives and supplied candidates; score repeated-item positives when present rather than unconditionally suppressing every seen item. [Author training and evaluation code](https://github.com/FeiSun/BERT4Rec/blob/master/run.py).
